name: A Survey on Self-Evolution of Large Language Models
authors: Zhengwei Tao, Ting-En Lin, Xiancai Chen, Hangyu Li, Yuchuan Wu, Yongbin Li, Zhi Jin, Fei Huang, Dacheng Tao, Jingren Zhou et al. — lead affiliations: Peking University (Key Lab of HCST, School of Computer Science), Alibaba Group (Tongyi Lab / Conversation AI), and Nanyang Technological University. Work done while Zhengwei Tao was interning at Alibaba.
venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CL / cs.AI); not peer-reviewed at time of writing (v1 22 Apr 2024, v2 3 Jun 2024)
code_url: https://github.com/AlibabaResearch/DAMO-ConvAI/tree/main/Awesome-Self-Evolution-of-LLM (curated reading list / awesome-list of self-evolution papers; no single method implementation)
reflection_type: survey/none (this is an analysis paper, not a method). It taxonomizes reflection-bearing approaches it reviews, spanning verbal-self-critique (Self-Refine, Reflexion, RCI, CRITIC), critique-free correction (STaR, Self-Debugging), learned/self-reward critics (Self-Reward, SIRLC, DLMA), tool/environment-verified feedback (Self-Debugging, CRITIC, SelfEvolve), and multi-agent debate (ChatEval, Debates). The survey's own contribution is the conceptual framework, not a new reflection mechanism.
feedback_source: Survey-level: catalogs all sources. Its 'Feedback' axis (Sec 4.3) splits feedback into (1) Model feedback — self-generated, e.g. self-as-judge / self-reward (Self-Reward, SIRLC, CAI, Self-Refine, Self-Alignment) and (2) Environment feedback — external tool/interpreter/compiler, search, simulated or real environments, unit tests, and reward signals (SelfEvolve, Self-Debugging, Reflexion, CRITIC, RoboCat, SOTOPIA-pi). Ground-truth/human supervision is framed as the costly status quo that self-evolution aims to reduce.
iteration_structure: Defines self-evolution as iterative cycles: at iteration t the model picks an evolution objective E^t, acquires experience (tasks, solutions, feedback), refines it, updates itself, and evaluates — feeding the next objective E^{t+1}. So the canonical structure is iterative-refine / episodic loops; the surveyed literature also includes single-shot refine, tree/search, and population/evolutionary (model-merging) methods. Notes that current methods empirically struggle to improve beyond ~3 self-evolution rounds.
reflection_object: Survey spans the full spectrum and explicitly factors 'Updating' into In-Weight vs In-Context. Objects reflected on / modified include: output content and reasoning chains/rationales (refinement, STaR), action trajectories (agent methods), prompt/context and external memory notes/rules (working & external memory: Reflexion, TRAN, MoT, IML, ICE, MemGPT), structured rules/constitutions (CAI, TRAN), model weights (replay/regularization/architecture updates: ReST, InstructGPT, LoRA, model soups, EvoLLM), and even model architecture/merging (Model Soups, UltraFuser, EvoLLM model merging).
requires_training: Survey covers the full range. Its 'Updating' taxonomy explicitly contrasts In-Weight updating (SFT via replay e.g. ReST/ReSTEM/SOTOPIA-pi/LLM2LLM; RL/preference e.g. InstructGPT-style RLHF, WARM, DLMA; regularization e.g. Elastic Reset, FuseLLM; architecture e.g. LoRA/ConPET/Model Soups/EvoLLM) against In-Context updating (external + working memory, no weight change). Thus: none | SFT | RL | DPO/preference | continual/regularized updates are all in scope.
reward_or_critic_model: All variants surveyed: none, self-as-judge (LLM-as-a-judge), trained reward models (reward-score selection / best-checkpoint selection per InstructGPT, WARM), verifiable/environment reward (tool, interpreter, env), and self-reward (Self-Reward, SIRLC, DLMA). The survey notes self-critics that have NOT co-evolved with the objective as a key reason self-evolution stalls after a few rounds.
distillation_target: Survey identifies multiple distillation/persistence forms under Updating: episodic-memory and reflected rationales/rules stored in external memory (MoT, MemoryBank, TiM, IML, ICE, TRAN, MemGPT); working-memory context (Reflexion, Agent-Pro, ProAgent); structured rules/constitutions (CAI, TRAN); prompts (PromptBreeder); and model-weights (replay/regularization/architecture-based in-weight updating, including model merging). It is the only survey field where 'all of the above' applies.
emergent_vs_engineered: Predominantly engineered/scaffolded — the surveyed pipeline (acquire-refine-update-evaluate with human-designed modules) is overwhelmingly prompt/framework-engineered. The survey's autonomy taxonomy (Low/Medium/High) frames current work as Low-level (humans design every module f); Medium/High autonomy (model designs its own evolution pipeline; emergent self-diagnosis) is posed as an open problem and the ultimate goal, not yet achieved. Predates o1/R1, so RL-emergent reflection ('aha') is not a central theme.
memory_type: Survey covers all: none, short-term/scratchpad (working memory), long-term-episodic and structured-notes/rules (external memory), skill/experience repositories, and playbook/rule cheatsheets. Updating Sec 6.2 splits memory into External Memory (collect/update/retrieve past experiences & reflected rationales) and Working Memory (in-context state used within the agent loop, e.g. Reflexion).
memory_persistence: Spans within-episode (working memory), cross-episode and cross-task (external memory of experiences/rationales, e.g. MemoryBank, MemGPT, IML, TRAN), up to longer-lived stores. The iterative cycle is inherently cross-episode/cross-task since refined experience is carried into subsequent iterations.
memory_curation_mechanism: Survey catalogs operations on external memory in a table (Table 2): Insert, Reflect, and Forget. MoT/TiM are insert-only (append-like); TRAN/IML/ICE/AesopAgent add Reflect (curate/summarize rules from experience); MemoryBank and MemGPT add Forget (eviction / FIFO rolling history) to keep memory bounded. So mechanisms surveyed include append-only, self-summarized/curated (reflect), and overwrite/forget (eviction).
error_localization_granularity: Survey-level (covers all granularities). Its Experience Refinement axis includes instance-level filtering/correcting and the Evaluation section contrasts instance-level critic/reflection with coarser task-/model-level qualitative evaluation, noting task/model-level critique is still underdeveloped. Methods reviewed range from holistic/outcome-level (filtering, self-consistency) to response-level (Self-Refine), step/trajectory-level (agent trajectory methods), and code block-level (Self-Debugging, LDB).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: Both. Intra-task refinement (refine a single task's solution, e.g. Self-Refine, Self-Debugging, iterative refinement) and inter-task transfer of distilled experience across tasks/iterations (Reflexion, IML, TRAN, ExpeL-style memory, ReST replay into weights) are both within the 'experience acquisition -> refinement -> updating' cycle, which is explicitly designed to carry experience forward across iterations and tasks.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: Survey covers all modes. Negative-experience methods (RLCD, DLMA, contrastive/perturbative solutions, COTERRORSET) and rule-from-mistakes memory (TRAN) emphasize avoidance of repeated errors in future episodes; iterative/critique-based correcting (Self-Refine, Reflexion, Self-Debugging) covers post-hoc and mid-trajectory revision. Not framed as a single method's choice; presented across the taxonomy.
task_domains: General/cross-domain survey: code, math, QA/reasoning, tool-use, web/embodied agents, dialogue (diagnostic dialogue, social skills, role-playing), decision-making, and general alignment/safety. Evolution directions enumerated: Improving Performance, Adaptation to Feedback, Expansion of Knowledge Base, and Safety/Ethics/Bias reduction.
benchmarks: As a survey it does not run a unified benchmark; it references representative tasks/benchmarks used by surveyed methods (e.g. reasoning GSM8K/MATH-style, code HumanEval/MBPP-style, agent/social environments such as ALFWorld, SOTOPIA, and instruction/tool-use benchmarks like UltraTool, T-Eval). For Evaluation it discusses dynamic LLM-based benchmarks (e.g. Sotopia) as a future direction over static benchmarks. No single headline benchmark table of its own.
headline_result: No empirical headline result — this is a conceptual/analysis survey, not an evaluated method. Its primary contribution is a unified conceptual framework defining self-evolution as iterative cycles of four phases (experience acquisition, experience refinement, updating, evaluation), plus a taxonomy of evolution objectives/abilities and per-module method taxonomies, and an identification of open problems (objective diversity/hierarchy, levels of autonomy, theoretical grounding, stability-plasticity, evaluation, safety/superalignment).
baselines: n/a (survey; no experimental baselines). Conceptually positions self-evolution against the prevailing paradigm of learning from costly human/external-model supervision, arguing the latter faces performance ceilings and cost limits as task complexity/diversity grows.
gains_vs_baseline: n/a — no quantitative delta reported by the survey itself. The argued qualitative 'gain' is scalability: self-generated-experience learning reduces dependence on human/teacher supervision and offers a potential path to scale LLMs toward superintelligence, though the survey cautions this is unproven and theoretically under-grounded.
compute_cost_profile: Not quantified as a single number. The survey argues a key motivation for self-evolution is reducing the cost of human/external-model supervision, and explicitly notes In-Context updating (memory) enables 'fast adaptive updates without expensive training costs' versus In-Weight updating which requires gradient/training compute. No inference-multiplier or rollout-count figures are given.
known_limitations: Survey's own Open Problems (Sec 8): (1) Objectives are narrow vs the vast space of human needs and lack hierarchical structure; (2) Most frameworks are Low-autonomy (every module hand-designed), needing human effort and not deployment-efficient — Medium/High autonomy is unsolved; (3) Lack of theoretical grounding — self-improvement mechanisms unclear, mixed evidence on whether LLMs self-correct without external feedback, risk of reduced diversity / 'model collapse' / self-consuming training loops, and methods empirically stall after ~3 rounds; (4) Updating faces the stability-plasticity dilemma (catastrophic forgetting vs adaptation); (5) Static benchmarks become unreliable, need dynamic/evolving evaluation; (6) Safety & superalignment of increasingly autonomous, self-evolving systems.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: Survey treats external/environment feedback vs intrinsic self-feedback as a central, contested axis. It explicitly cites the mixed evidence: Huang et al. observed self-corrective behavior in models >22B parameters, while Ganguli et al. found LLMs struggle to self-correct reasoning errors WITHOUT external feedback. The 'Feedback' module separates Model (self) feedback from Environment (external/verifiable) feedback, acknowledging external/verifiable signals are often what makes self-evolution work.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / contested (per the survey). It reports mixed results in the literature: self-correction/self-improvement can be net-positive in some settings (e.g. large models, with feedback) but unreliable without external feedback; further, repeated self-evolution tends to plateau or degrade after a few rounds (hypothesized: self-critic has not co-evolved with the objective), and training on self-generated data risks diversity loss and model collapse.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The survey predates the o1/R1 reasoning-model 'reasoning tax' calibration discourse and does not analyze calibration/overconfidence of reflective self-correction; it instead frames reliability via the external-feedback dependency and model-collapse risks.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a — this is a self-evolution survey, not a failure-attribution method. It does discuss failure-relevant phenomena (self-correction failure without external feedback, model collapse, self-evolution plateau after ~3 rounds, stability-plasticity/catastrophic forgetting) but does not classify or attribute failures via a taxonomy of multi-agent failure modes.
failure_mode_addressed: Failure modes discussed (not in MAST's 14-mode taxonomy terms): superficial/ineffective self-reflection and inability to self-correct reasoning errors without external feedback; error accumulation in self-consuming training loops / model collapse; reduced output diversity from self-generated data; self-evolution stagnation after limited iterations (self-critic not co-evolving with objective); catastrophic forgetting (stability-plasticity dilemma); and safety/alignment failures (bias, superalignment) of autonomous systems.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset or benchmark released. The artifact is a curated GitHub reading list (Awesome-Self-Evolution-of-LLM) of surveyed papers; the survey advocates for future dynamic/evolving benchmarks (citing Sotopia) but does not contribute one.
builds_on: Synthesizes foundational self-improvement/self-correction work it reviews, including: 'Large Language Models Can Self-Improve' (Huang et al., LMSI), STaR (Zelikman et al.), Self-Refine (Madaan et al.), Reflexion (Shinn et al.), RCI, CRITIC, Self-Debugging, Self-Instruct (Wang et al.), Constitutional AI / Self-Alignment (Bai et al.; Sun et al. Dromedary), Self-Reward, ReST / ReST-EM (self-training), and memory frameworks (MemGPT, MemoryBank, TRAN, IML/In-Memory Learning). Conceptually inspired by human experiential learning.
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by and inspires subsequent self-evolution work, e.g. AgentGym / AgentEvol (Xi et al.), R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data (Huang et al.), Guided Self-Evolving LLMs / R-Few (Yu et al.), RISE (self-evolving VLMs), PACE (two-timescale self-evolution for small LM agents), CoMAS (co-evolving multi-agent systems), Alita-G (self-evolving generative agent), Evolving LLMs' Self-Refinement (EvolVE), and later surveys/roadmaps (Lifelong Learning of LLM-based Agents roadmap; Evolutionary Computation in the Era of LLMs; A Survey on Complex Reasoning of LLMs through the Lens of Self-Evolution; Evo-Memory benchmark; LLM-Evolve).
citation_count: ~70 (Semantic Scholar, Corpus ID 269294023, as fetched; 155 references; an earlier cached snapshot showed 62). Treat as approximate and growing.
on_policy_distillation_link: Relevant in spirit but not by name: the survey's In-Weight 'Replay-based' updating (ReST / ReST-EM, self-training on filtered self-generated rollouts) is closely related to on-policy/self-distillation and skill-optimization ideas, and it frames self-evolution as iteratively distilling refined self-generated experience back into weights or memory. It predates and does not cite the specific 'on-policy distillation' formulation.
sample_efficiency: Not quantified as trials-to-gain. The survey reports a qualitative empirical observation that current self-evolution methods struggle to improve after roughly three rounds of self-evolution, suggesting limited iterative sample efficiency / diminishing returns.
